original_value: Computational thinking is increasingly treated as a foundational skill across schooling. Building on both curriculum-focused and city-scale implementation studies, this article synthesizes evidence on how computational thinking can be introduced in primary education, with emphasis on teacher development, classroom integration, and practical barriers to scale. The review also identifies research gaps and outlines design considerations for future curriculum work.

The review also highlights research gaps and sets out design considerations for future curriculum work.
